messages:
alex: quick follow-up on the packaging RFC — we need to pick a concrete path for on-prem/air-gapped bundles. main tradeoffs: OCI-layered images vs signed tarballs, delta vs full updates, and how verification should work when there's no outbound network. any preferences?

priya: +1 to designing for signed artifact bundles that can be transported (usb/scp). OCI is nice but air-gapped ops really want a single file drop. propose: signed tar.gz bundle + a small manifest with component SHAs and provenance. keep deltas optional. :thought_balloon:

mikael: runtime note: side-by-side installs avoid hot-upgrade complexity. if we allow in-place patching, we must constrain ABI changes strictly. suggested compat scheme: semantic component matrix, e.g. runtime v1.x compatible with model-plugin v1.x only. also we should version kv cache layout separately.

priya: agree on manifest. example manifest we discussed: 
```json
{
  "bundle_version": "2026-03-17",
  "components": [
    {"name": "inference-runtime", "version": "1.4.2", "sha256": "aa..."},
    {"name": "model-store", "version": "0.9.7", "sha256": "bb..."}
  ],
  "compat": {"min_runtime": "1.4.0", "max_runtime": "2.0.0"},
  "provenance": {"signed_by": "redwood-release@company", "slsa": "v1"}
}
```

jamie: ops concerns: how do we handle DB migrations in air-gapped upgrades? big migrations need a maintenance window. prefer: decouple schema migrations into separate step with preview mode and automatic rollback if migration fails. also support canary by running side-by-side and shifting traffic.

mikael: +1 on canary side-by-side. Implementation detail: installer should accept `--install-mode=side-by-side|inplace` and validate disk/port overlaps. Side-by-side pattern: install to /opt/redwood/releases/<release-id> and symlink current -> release-id after health checks. rollback = switch symlink back.

alex: good. what about delta updates? we could support binary diffs (bsdiff/zygote) but verification harder. maybe deltas only for non-breaking patches and always include a full bundle fallback.

priya: deltas make sense for bandwidth-limited customers but keep them optional and gated. metadata should include diff base SHA and patch SHA. installer should refuse delta if base mismatch.

sec-bot: security note: signing and key rotation. mandate: cosign-compatible signatures + optional HSM/KMS backing. rotation flow: release keys live in CIP/KMS; customers can provide their own signing key for private builds. must record key id in manifest. consider PKCS#11 for on-prem HSM support.

opsbot: reminder: per airgap policy 3.2 we need USB seed image workflow and a signed verification tool bundled separately. also log that offline verification requires an offline trust store shipped with the bundle or pre-provisioned on the appliance.

alex: proposed minimal spec for next RFC patch: 1) bundle = signed tar.gz + manifest.json + signatures (cosign), 2) support full and optional delta bundles, 3) installer modes: side-by-side and in-place with `--install-mode`, 4) manifest fields: components[], compat matrix, provenance (key id, slsa), 5) verification: sha256 + signature + optional HSM path, 6) DB migrations split into preview + apply phases.

priya: volunteer to draft updated manifest schema and sample CLI install flows.

mikael: I'll draft the installer state machine (side-by-side, health checks, rollback).

jamie: ops runbook updates from me — maintenance window examples and metrics to guard on (latency, error rate).

deploy-bot: RFC: packaging-spec-v2 pushed to /rfc/packaging/spec-v2.md — preview link: https://internal.redwood/rfc/packaging/spec-v2 (no external access) :rocket:

alex: thanks all. action items above. we'll sync next Tue 10am to finalize and fold into the RFC. If anyone has strong objections to tar.gz+cosign approach, speak up now.

priya: none from me. leaning into SLSA provenance for audits.

mikael: fine from infra side. just be explicit about ABI compat checks.

jamie: fine. ops will prepare a checklist for offline validation.

alex: closing thread for now — will incorporate PR comments into the RFC. :thumbsup:
